Data Science
  

  • DS 7020: Introductory SAS Programming for Data Science

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Admission to the Data Science and Analytics, MS program
    Students will learn how to use SAS programming for data science and analytics tasks such as data importation, manipulation, summarization, and communication through various means at both an introductory and intermediate level.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Import data of various file types (e.g., CSV, XLSX, TXT).
    2. Evaluate data structure through various means (e.g., PROC CONTENTS, PROC PRINT).
    3. Manipulate data tables in various ways, which may include column selection, row filtering, BY group processing, and DO loops.
    4. Interpret common error messages and learn how to correct them.
    5. Produce reports using ODS statements which include output from SAS procedures.
  

  • DS 7120: Advanced Programming in SAS

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: STAT 7100  and DS 7020  
    This course will cover advanced programming techniques using the SAS system for data management and statistical analysis. The topics covered include macro programming, using SQL with SAS and optimizing SAS programs. Upon completion of this course students will be prepared to take and pass the certification test and obtain the Advanced Programmer for SAS 9 certification.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Generate detail reports by working with a single table, joining tables, or using set operators in SQL.
    2. Generate summary reports by working with a single table, joining tables, or using set operators in the SQL.
    3. Construct sub-queries and in-line views within an SQL procedure step.
    4. Use SAS SQL procedure enhancements. 
    5. Create and use user-defined and automatic macro variables within the SAS Macro Language. 
    6. Automate programs by defining and calling macros using the SAS Macro Language. 
    7. Use macro functions. 
    8. Debug Macros. 
    9. Create data-driven programs using SAS Macro Language. 
    10. Process data using 1 and 2 dimensional arrays. 
    11. Process data using hash objects. 
    12. Use SAS utility procedures. 
    13. Use Advanced functions. 
  

  • DS 7130: Programming in R

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Admission to the Data Science and Analytics, MS program 
    Students will learn how to use the R programming language inside of an appropriate integrated development environment (IDE) for file management, data manipulation, transformation, analysis, visualization and communication as these concepts relate to data science and analytical tasks. Students will also learn intermediate R programming tasks potentially including iteration and simulation.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Manipulate dataframes including selecting columns, filtering rows, creating new variables, aggregating data, and merging tables using modern R programming techniques.
    2. Generate high-quality data visualizations using modern R visualization packages.
    3. Compile Word/PDF documents that render text, code, and output using integrated text compiling methods.
    4. Perform iterative programming tasks using both traditional and modern approaches.
    5. Use R to perform and generate output for various statistical analyses, including but not limited to: descriptive statistics, factorial ANOVA, and text mining.
  

  • DS 7140: Python for Data Science

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Admission to the Data Science and Analytics, MS program.
    This course introduces students to Python, including data preparation, feature engineering and general use of Python libraries with a focus on applications within the realm of Data Science. The core focus is the development of Python skills to enable the preparation of data and custom functions, to support Data Science model development activities. Students will learn fundamental data structures, key algorithms and their application in applying analytic/machine learning methodologies.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Configure and manage Python environment for various analytics tasks.
    2. Install and update Python and associated add-on packages on each environment.
    3. Perform basic object-oriented computing using list, dictionary, matrices, arrays, and Dataframes.
    4. Import and export data into and from Python using various data file protocols.
    5. Perform basic data management tasks including recoding variables, converting data types, merging data, etc.
    6. Perform intermediate computing tasks such as using conditional processing statements, loops, the apply family of functions, and writing one’s own functions.
    7. Perform basic and advanced graphing of data.
    8. Use statistical functions in Python.
    9. Perform basic predictive and descriptive modeling of data.
    10. Generate pseudo-random data.
    11. Write customized simulation programs. 
  

  • DS 7240: Applied Data Mining

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: STAT 7210  or IT 7103  
    Data Mining is an information extraction activity whose goal is to discover hidden facts contained in databases and perform prediction and forecasting through interaction with data. The process includes data selection, cleaning and coding, using statistical pattern recognition and machine learning techniques, and reporting and visualization of the generated structures. The course will cover all these issues with the emphasis on practical applications. Students will be encouraged to use recent Data Mining software.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Explore the data sets under the context of the business problem with existing data mining software.
    2. Clean and prepare the data for modeling with existing data mining software.
    3. Build various models according to the nature of the business problem and compare them using the chosen software.
    4. Communicate the results clearly in writing and orally.
  

  • DS 7800: Research in Data Science and Analytics

    1-3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Permission of MSDSA Program Coordinator
    This course offers MS in Data Science and Analytics students the opportunity to conduct academic research under faculty mentorship. Students will investigate advanced and/or applied topics, contribute to ongoing projects, and collaborate in the development of original scholarly work. Emphasis is placed on the research process, which may include literature review, methodology, analysis, and writing. The ultimate course goal is the production of a scholarly product suitable for dissemination through academic venues such as journals, conferences, or symposia.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to:

    1. Demonstrate competency in the scholarly research process by contributing meaningfully to an academic study and/or producing a scholarly product under faculty supervision.
    2. Apply appropriate analytical techniques and tools to collect, process, and interpret data in support of a clearly defined research question or hypothesis.
    3. Produce and/or present scholarly work that meets standards for academic dissemination, including formats suitable for peer-reviewed publication or conference presentation.
  

  • DS 7900: Applied Analytics Project Course

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: STAT 7210  or permission of the instructor
    This is a highly applied project course using real data. Students will be broken into teams for the semester and will work together to design, execute, and present an analysis to address the sponsor’s business problem. There will be regular feedback sessions with the instructors and client as the semester progresses. The class closely mimics what students will experience when they work on projects in a job setting. Typically, the course will have an external project sponsor.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Communicate analysis plans and results in a professional manner through written mediums.
    2. Communicate analysis plans and results in a professional manner through oral presentations.
    3. Effectively work in a team environment to successfully complete a data analytics project.
  

  • DS 7918: Internship

    1-3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Permission of Program Director.
    Students engage with an employer in a hired experience where their responsibilities and day-to-day tasks involve data science activities as agreed upon by the student, the employer, and the program director.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Develop skills in collecting, cleaning, organizing and managing data using appropriate tools and techniques.

    2. Apply and evaluate appropriate statistical and/or machine learning methods to address organizational problems.

    3. Present findings effectively while collaborating with teams/partners within and/or outside the organization.
  

  • DS 7940: Applied Analysis Project

    1-9 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Permission of the program director.
    Students will work with a school faculty member on a project involving data science and/or analytics techniques in application. The student and faculty member will agree upon the scope of the project and the deliverables at the beginning of the semester. The student will then work under the supervision of the faculty member to produce the agreed upon deliverables by the end of the term.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Define the goals of a project including relevant variables if approrpriate.
    2. Appropriately perform preliminary work which may include data cleaning/preprocessing and/or review of relevant literature.
    3. Use approrpriate methods to address the goals of the project.
    4. Appropriately interpret the results of the analysis and communicate the findings in a professional manner. The communication of the results may include white papers, poster presentations, and manuscript submissions.
  

  • DS 7950: Applied Consulting for Data Science and Analytics

    3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: STAT 7210 
    This applied project course offers hands-on, consulting-style experience. Students will work in teams to execute the full data science workflow, including data acquisition, analysis, modeling, and communication of results. The curriculum emphasizes professional skills, including client engagement, project management, and presenting findings to non-technical audiences. Students will collaborate to produce client-facing deliverables and prepare for collaborative, real-world roles in data science and analytics.

    Note: This course may be repeated for up to 6 credit hours.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to:

    1. Apply data science and analytical techniques to solve practical problems in a team context.
    2. Communicate analytical findings clearly and professionally in multiple formats.
    3. Collaborate effectively in team-based environments.
    4. Manage project timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder expectations.
  

  • DS 9000: Advanced Special Topics in Data Science

    1-3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Admission to the Ph.D. in Data Science and Analytics program
    This is a doctoral level seminar course which will cover selected contemporary topics in data science of interest and relevance to faculty and students.
  

  • DS 9700: Doctoral Internship

    1-6 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Ph.D. candidacy.
    The doctoral internship in data science and analytics provides a supervised experience in research and professional practice. It offers doctoral students the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world situations, develop advanced research and problem-solving skills, and gain valuable insights into their future careers. 
  

  • DS 9800: Advanced Research in Data Science and Analytics

    1 - 3 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: By permission of instructor.
    This course allows students to conduct research under an advisor, is designed to explore research areas, and mentors for dissertations.

    Note: This is not dissertation hours and is intended for use in special circumstances.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Research and critique the current literature to develop a research question or identify a gap in the literature.
    2. Conduct an independent research project to address the research question or gap.
    3. Develop a scholarly product such as a manuscript, conference presentation, or poster related to the research project.
  

  • DS 9900: PhD Dissertation Research

    1-9 Credit Hours
    Prerequisite: Progression to candidacy and permission of the instructor.
    This course includes dissertation writing under the direction of the major professor (dissertation advisor). The course is taught using a non-traditional format of independent research and preparation of the doctoral dissertation.

    Course Learning Outcomes
    Students who successfully complete this course will be able to: 

    1. Demonstrate a range of skills appropriate for an independent researcher in data science or analytics.
    2. Present their research substantively in written form through a series of iterative drafts.
    3. Accept and incorporate feedback from advisor and committee members into written drafts.
    4. Demonstrate consistent progress in their research and writing by continuously producing written work.
    5. Successfully present their dissertation research in a dissertation proposal defense/dissertation defense to a public audience.
